clue.text: It could play music in USA: Simply Red's best CD released

indicators.note: something released is set free from its fixed form, so the letters are let loose to regroup

parts.note: the nineteen letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast that Simply Red's greatest-hits album has come out in America and would suit any stereo.
explanation.walkthrough: Simply Red is a British pop band, which makes 'best CD released' read as an album launch rather than an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudspeaker setup in a hall or station is used for announcements and can equally broadcast recorded songs.

clue.text: Conservative supporting column by party researcher

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting element sits underneath, so the party word goes below the earlier pieces

parts.note: a post is an upright column
a do is a party or celebration
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political researcher backs a Conservative newspaper column for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists C first, but 'supporting' places it at the bottom of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is an academic doing research after completing a doctorate, so researcher is a fair general description.

clue.text: Bark on this Labrador upset it

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down light the short dog word is flipped end to end

parts.note: a Lab is short for a Labrador retriever
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A dog getting agitated and barking at some tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark looks like a dog's noise or a tree's skin, but here it is a barque, a sailing boat. 'It' meaning sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood used to build rafts, so a small boat could be floated on it.

clue.text: Cutting off oil giant's supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stopping the flow of petroleum from a major energy company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the noun for the oil delivery; it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolating something separates it from others, the same as severing its connections or cutting it off.

clue.text: See 1
Adult on drink clutching sober partner

parts.note: A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip something tightly, so the drink word holds the sober word inside it

parts.note: a common drink
TT is teetotal, never drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A grown-up who has been drinking clings to a partner who stayed dry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, adult sitting 'on' the rest puts A at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter helps another person carry out a deed, usually a crime, making them an accomplice or partner.

clue.text: Empty drawer containing ice cube? One might

indicators.note: emptying a word strips out its interior, leaving only the outside letters as a shell
containing means holding inside, so the frozen water word goes into the shell

parts.note: the outer letters only, with its middle removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empty freezer drawer with only one ice cube in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'cube? One might': a kitchen tool that cubes vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A dicer is a gadget that chops food into small cubes, so dicing is cubing.

clue.text: Get grease in bits: it may be found by a child in spring

definitions.text: it may be found by a child in spring

indicators.note: broken into bits, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child gets grease all over themselves while playing outdoors in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring here is the season, when children hunt for hidden chocolate eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Children search gardens for hidden chocolate eggs at Easter, which falls in spring.

clue.text: See 1 across
Worries about the first dental problem

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worries word goes round the numeral

parts.note: cares are worries
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: Someone frets mainly about their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' gives I as Roman one, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical name for tooth decay, a common dental complaint.

clue.text: Handle books: take off sticker

parts.note: to handle goods is to deal in or sell them
OT is the Old Testament, a group of books
to take off someone is to mimic or ape them

explanation.surface: Instructions for dealing with books: remove the label stuck on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Sellotape is the British brand name for clear sticky tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive tape is used to fasten things together, so it is literally a sticker.

clue.text: Way boss ultimately added to company expenses

indicators.note: added to means joined on after, so the pieces are placed behind the firm word

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company
ST is street, a way

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the last letter of boss

explanation.surface: The way the boss ended up adding to the firm's running costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs are outgoings or charges incurred, the same as expenses.

clue.text: Play a shot in the lead

indicators.note: being in the lead means going in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a dram is a shot of whisky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports report: a single shot put one side in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is the definition, a stage play, not a sporting move.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on stage, radio or screen.

clue.text: Step in time, free rein when dancing to provide entertainment

indicators.note: to entertain is also to hold a guest, so the jumbled letters host the time letter
dancing letters move about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to a dancer: step in time and let yourself go to entertain the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step in time' sounds like dance instruction, but 'Step in' alone is the definition and time is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to get involved uninvited, which is what interfering means.

clue.text: Caught child's toes dropping piano: they may get put out by foot

definitions.text: they may get put out by foot

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: piggies is nursery talk for toes, from 'this little piggy'
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A child's toes get caught and they drop the piano on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Ciggies is British slang for cigarettes, stubbed out underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarettes are often extinguished by stamping on the stub with a shoe, so a foot puts them out.

clue.text: Newly-wed carrying on with nurse in place behind the scenes?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the newly-wed word bears the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a groom has just married
re means on, as in concerning
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A newly married man carrying on with a nurse somewhere out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like an affair, but carrying is the insertion and 'on' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A green room is the lounge where performers wait offstage, literally behind the scenery.

clue.text: Substitute with rest punching match official

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so the rest word is driven inside the official word

parts.note: a ref is a referee
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A football substitute, after a rest, punches the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a replacement worker or player who takes over from another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Small type of cow: one with disease

parts.note: a cow lows, so it is a lower, one that moos
a case is a patient, a person who has an illness

explanation.surface: A farmer describes a small breed of cow that has caught an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small type of cow' reads like a breed, but 'Small type' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower case letters are the small, non-capital forms in printing type.

clue.text: Load of women with a curvy figure

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for women
the numeral 8 is all curves

explanation.surface: A lot of women with curvaceous figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a body shape but means a digit.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy object being carried or borne, which is what a load is.

clue.text: Heading for court, if Trump is lying about deal

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction
a heading is at the top, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of court
taken as written
in British slang, to trump is to break wind

explanation.surface: A news line about a president facing court and lying about a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the president here but British slang for breaking wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade, especially illegally, so it means to deal in goods.

clue.text: Have sex with risk? Her husband is late

parts.note: slang: to do someone is to have sex with them
a wager is a bet, a risk

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a risky encounter; then a remark about a woman whose husband has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like running behind schedule; it means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her deceased spouse.

clue.text: Boring date — back on eHarmony, ultimately

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so pieces follow in order downward

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for date
the rear is the back

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the dating site is kept

parts.note: the last letter of eHarmony

explanation.surface: A dull date, and so it is back to the online dating site in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: eHarmony is an online dating service, which suits the dull date in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and tedious, just as something boring is.

clue.text: Accept once more a duke in post

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the post word

parts.note: to remit money is to send or post it
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke is taken back into an official position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job; it is the verb to send.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to let them in again, to accept them back.

clue.text: Stand during reckoning: what might come out of one's mouth?

definitions.text: what might come out of one's mouth?

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the stand word sits within the reckoning word

parts.note: a sum is a calculation, a reckoning
to stand something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: Standing up during a day of reckoning, wondering what to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the phrase suggests words but means spit and phlegm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is mucus coughed up and spat from the mouth.

clue.text: Bore to compose film score

parts.note: to pen is to write or compose
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien
to rate something is to score it

explanation.surface: A dull person sets out to write music for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person but is the verb, to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore through something is to drill a hole into it, which is to penetrate it.

clue.text: Lifting toe on foot, hard for the old

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping them, so one letter replaces the other in the toe word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
O is an abbreviation for old
FT is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Raising an elderly person's toe on to their foot is hard for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifting is slang for stealing; H takes the place of O in toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is informal for stealing it, so lifting is theft.

clue.text: Mostly stick on port wine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the stick word is dropped

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port
to stick is to jab

explanation.surface: Mostly stick to port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port wine' reads as one drink, but port is the city and wine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Love song around noon playing on the radio

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the love and song pieces surround the noon letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
an air is a tune
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A love song about midday is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being broadcast live, as when heard on the radio.

clue.text: Figure of speech from Hamlet's closing line

indicators.note: closing means at the end, so only the final letter of the play's hero is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Hamlet
a line is a rope

explanation.surface: A famous rhetorical phrase from the final line of Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closing line' suggests the play's last words, but closing takes one letter and line is a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of language such as a metaphor, a figure of speech.

clue.text: Shoot gangster? Weapon that might be raised with smoke

definitions.text: that might be raised with smoke

parts.note: to fire is to shoot
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gangster scene: shoot, then raise a smoking gun.
explanation.walkthrough: A raised weapon with smoke evokes a gun just fired; it is an alarm raised on detecting smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is sounded, or raised, when smoke signals a blaze.

clue.text: Mock exam's last part: writer's quote is the wrong way round

indicators.note: the last part of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of exam
the writer's is I'm, the setter referring to themselves

indicators.note: the wrong way round means back to front, so the quote word runs backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A student finishing a mock exam realises their quotation is backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock exam' looks like a practice test; Mock alone is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetic means imitative, copying something, as a mock version imitates the real thing.

clue.text: Hidden camp housing soldiers

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so the camp word holds the soldiers inside

parts.note: a camp is a faction or sect
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A concealed military camp with troops inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' suggests a military base, but it means a group sharing a view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is kept out of sight or knowledge, which means hidden.
